title: Still True
tagline: Your AI didn't hallucinate. The world changed. A send-gate that catches facts that expired before you hit send.
phase: Not entered on its own: its engine is the safeguard inside Why-Now Wire
bottomLine: Not entered as its own product. Its verification engine (exact quotes re-found on the page, dated sources, rules in code) is the safeguard inside Why-Now Wire, the lead path. The send-gate idea stands for later: catching facts that expired between when the AI learned them and when you hit send.
healthReason: Parked for the day, not dropped: the engine ships inside the lead path.
why: Hallucination detectors check an answer against the documents it was given. None of them notices when a fact was true at training time and has since changed. In sales that is the email congratulating a buyer on a funding round that was superseded last week. In a first-party probe on 13 November, a model answering without search was out of date on most of a dozen companies picked because they had recently changed. The sample was selected for change, so it shows the failure exists, not how often it happens.
mission: A send-gate for AI-drafted outreach. Three searches per claim (neutral, counter-evidence, primary source), the pages re-read in full, the model returning only a stance label and a quote, and plain code deciding the verdict: the quote must be found on the page, every number in the claim must appear in the quote, newer credible evidence beats older, and an unknown source never decides. 'Can't confirm' is the default; every other verdict has to be earned.
destination: On stage, a model-written email is checked live, one claim flips to 'changed' with its quote and date, Send is refused, the fix is accepted and Send unlocks. Done when that runs end to end on a fresh draft generated that morning, and an eval against the no-search baseline is shown as counts.
showcase: Separating groundedness (matches the documents) from still-true (matches today's world), and building for the second
A fail-closed release gate: an HTTP refusal that names the blocking claims, overridable only by a named person with a logged reason
Rules in code rather than prompts, each verdict traceable to a rule, a quote and a page date
Exact matching on numbers, so a changed figure can never pass as close enough

milestones.title: Architecture, verdict rules and safeguards designed
Probe: do page dates match publish dates?
One claim end to end in the browser
Full draft checked live, Send refused, run saved as a replay
Re-check over time and baseline eval

assumptions.assumption: Page dates from search reflect when a story was published
assumptions.test: Compare them with known publish dates for recent stories; if two or more are wrong, recency comes only from dated data records

assumptions.assumption: Enough evidence sits outside paywalls to earn verdicts other than 'can't confirm'
assumptions.test: A command-line run on a fresh draft returns at least one 'changed' verdict with a quote verified on the page

risks.risk: Seen as one more fact-checker in a crowded track
risks.mitigation: Lead with time, not truth: the same claim checked as of last week and today, and a gate that refuses rather than a score

risks.risk: A crawl date mistaken for a publish date gives a wrong verdict on screen
risks.mitigation: Every verdict shows where its date came from; demo claims are picked from what the engine actually returns that morning

nextSteps.action: Revisit as a stand-alone send-gate after the event
